title: It Doesn’t Have To Be Crazy At Work

questions.q: What question does the book suggest asking about your company as a product?
a: How easy is it for employees to use, and where is it slow?
How much market share could it win this quarter?
How do its profits compare with competitors?
How quickly could it be sold to a buyer?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to look for slow spots and bugs, just as you would in software.

questions.q: What meeting change did Basecamp make?
a: It replaced status meetings with written updates
It shortened every meeting to ten minutes
It banned meetings before noon each day
It required managers to attend every meeting
questions.why: Lesson 2 says progress reports go into company software for others to read when convenient.

questions.q: Why does the summary compare a workday to a long flight?
a: The office has far more interruptions than a plane
Both leave people too tired to think clearly
Both require strict schedules to run smoothly
The plane offers better food and more rest
questions.why: Lesson 2 says flights are free of the constant interruptions and pointless meetings found at work.

questions.q: How did Basecamp test a big price increase safely?
a: It charged new customers only and kept old prices
It surveyed thousands of customers first
It tested the price in one small country
It offered refunds to anyone who complained
questions.why: Lesson 3 says raising the price only for new clients let the company roll it back if it failed.

questions.q: What is the book's view of working more than 40 hours a week?
a: It is treated as honorable but is really a sign of insanity
It is necessary for ambitious young employees
It is the only way to beat competitors
It should be rewarded with extra vacation
questions.why: The overview says overwork is treated like a badge of honor when it is really a sign of insanity.
